M01.title: Safety precautions
M01.studyTask: Use the safety chapter alongside current first-aid, OSHA and electrical safety guidance.

M02.title: Basic mathematics for electronics
M02.studyTask: Review units, powers of ten and quantities, then explain one numerical conversion.

M02.title: DC circuits
M02.studyTask: Connect voltage and electric current to the atom and DC-circuit models.

M03.title: Basic mathematics for electronics
M03.studyTask: Work the publisher examples on Ohm’s law and power and check your own unit conversions.

M03.title: Electronic components
M03.studyTask: Identify resistor families, ratings and the difference between nominal value and real construction.

M04.title: DC circuits
M04.studyTask: Use the chapter’s DC circuit examples to justify series, parallel and divider calculations.

M05.title: Diagnostic techniques
M05.studyTask: Interpret an actual interconnection or block diagram before checking a meter or circuit.

M05.title: Test equipment
M05.studyTask: Compare analog and digital meter use; choose the correct instrument for the measurement.

M06.title: Basic mathematics for electronics
M06.studyTask: Find the source discussion of waveforms, RMS values and frequency; sketch and label a cycle.

M06.title: Test equipment
M06.studyTask: Locate the oscilloscope description and explain probe and grounding precautions.

M07.title: Capacitance, inductance, transformers and filters
M07.studyTask: Compare capacitor, inductor and transformer behavior, and explain energy storage.

M07.title: Basic mathematics for electronics
M07.studyTask: Review RC time constants and reactive component calculations already introduced in Chapter 3.

M08.title: AC circuit operations
M08.studyTask: Solve an impedance/phase or AC-network example and consult the publisher corrections for pages 47–48.

M08.title: Capacitance, inductance, transformers and filters
M08.studyTask: Use the filters section to compare frequency-dependent behavior.

M09.title: Generators, alternators and motors
M09.studyTask: Explain motor/generator conversions and why changing flux matters.

M09.title: Capacitance, inductance, transformers and filters
M09.studyTask: Relate transformer core behavior to magnetic fields and induction.

M10.title: Basic mathematics for electronics
M10.studyTask: Use the time-constant introduction as prerequisite for timing and wave-shaping.

M10.title: Digital concepts and logic
M10.studyTask: Connect sequential logic and switching examples to later timing design; the guide does not necessarily cover every oscillator concept.

M11.title: Semiconductors
M11.studyTask: Review PN junctions and transistor families, applying corrections for printed page 74.

M12.title: Discrete solid-state circuits
M12.studyTask: Compare common solid-state circuit arrangements and common fault symptoms.

M12.title: Amplifiers, gain and decibels
M12.studyTask: Relate gain and bias concepts to transistor or IC amplifier stages.

M13.title: Electronic power supplies
M13.studyTask: Trace supply conversion from source through rectification, filtering and regulation.

M14.title: Amplifiers, gain and decibels
M14.studyTask: Practice amplifier gain, decibel and coupling examples with units and explicit ratios.

M15.title: Soldering, desoldering and PCB repair
M15.studyTask: Study safe solder, desoldering and PCB repair technique; paper study does not prove hands-on skill.

M16.title: Digital concepts and logic
M16.studyTask: Convert number representations and explain truth tables before moving into sequential logic.

M17.title: Digital concepts and logic
M17.studyTask: Review gates, flip-flops, counters and the official correction on printed page 138.

M18.title: Test equipment
M18.studyTask: Choose test equipment and describe a stepwise signal fault isolation strategy.

M18.title: Diagnostic techniques
M18.studyTask: Connect block-diagram use to troubleshooting sequence.

M19.title: Discrete solid-state circuits
M19.studyTask: Relate discrete circuit examples to signal-interface behavior.

M19.title: Test equipment
M19.studyTask: Review diagnostic measurement choices; the full interoperability scope extends beyond this book.

M20.title: Microprocessors and controllers
M20.studyTask: Identify microprocessor/controller parts, control examples and debugging ideas.

M21.title: Microprocessors and controllers
M21.studyTask: Use programming and debugging foundations as prerequisite for software setup.

M21.title: Diagnostic techniques
M21.studyTask: Use technical information and manual-following skills; networking/security material may need other sources.

M22.title: Basic radio and RF
M22.studyTask: Review coaxial feedline principles and cable loss in RF applications.

M22.title: Transmitters
M22.studyTask: Review transmission-line and antenna connections; fiber, network cabling and crimp standards need additional sources.

M23.title: Test equipment
M23.studyTask: Explain what each bench instrument measures and when to choose it.

M24.title: Amplifiers, gain and decibels
M24.studyTask: Relate gain, audio signal paths and amplifier operation to AV systems.

M24.title: Telephone systems
M24.studyTask: Use telephony as a communications-system example; contemporary digital AV needs other sources.

M25.title: Semiconductors
M25.studyTask: Review optoelectronic devices and contrast emitted, detected and isolated light functions.

M26.title: Basic radio and RF
M26.studyTask: Study RF generation, tuning, antenna and impedance fundamentals.

M26.title: Transmitters
M26.studyTask: Connect RF fundamentals to actual transmitter building blocks.

M27.title: Telephone systems
M27.studyTask: Review the communications topology, signalling and telephone-system vocabulary.

M27.title: Transmitters
M27.studyTask: Compare transmitter blocks to related telecommunications signals.

M28.title: Diagnostic techniques
M28.studyTask: Use diagrams and manuals to plan a fault search and record the evidence.

M28.title: Record keeping and service management
M28.studyTask: Practice truthful records, service procedures and professional documentation.

M28.title: Technical writing
M28.studyTask: Write a short technical report with observations, procedure and conclusion.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Lockout, stored energy and verification
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Safety, electric shock, bench equipment and vintage devices are discussed; the old first-aid and energized-work recommendations must not substitute for modern professional guidance.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: After studying Alfred safety protocols, identify two unsafe assumptions in vintage bench or first-aid discussions. Apply current qualified procedures, not book-era examples.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: SI prefixes: communicating scale without losing units
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: The assigned pages cover math, engineering prefixes and electrical formulas; the opening page contains introduction as well as examples.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Convert three quantities between SI prefixes, write each result with its unit and check one power/Ohm-law relationship.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Comparing P = VI, I²R and V²/R
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed page 27 explicitly discusses power changes with resistance and current and DC circuit relationships.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: From P = I²R and P = V²/R, explain what is held constant before predicting how power changes.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Loaded divider: why a measurement or circuit changes Vout
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 27–31 present DC series/parallel resistor networks and a classic tube B+ voltage divider; a modern loaded-divider model needs additional Alfred instruction.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Compute the book series/parallel reduction, then use Alfred to include the loading resistance of a measured divider.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Schematic, wiring and layout: practice moving between views
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 161–162 concern schematic drawings, service information and symbolic circuit tracing.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Follow an input-to-output path using both a schematic and block diagram; identify where you would measure.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Capacitive and inductive reactance
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 19–22 contain capacitor calculations, time constants and reactive circuit reasoning, not a comprehensive modern capacitor construction/polarity survey.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Solve the book capacitor/reactance exercise. Revisit Alfred separately for polarized-device safety and component selection.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: From impedance to an equivalent circuit
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 45–49 discuss AC behavior, reactance and series/parallel circuit relationships. Official errata apply to some pages.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Identify the resistive and reactive contributions to impedance and predict how frequency alters current.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Motor and generator: opposite energy directions
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Chapter 7 printed pages 53–57 address generator, alternator and motor machines. This is not a first-use primer on transformer primary/secondary operation.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Compare a motor and a generator; explain how field and conductor motion affect the direction of energy conversion.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Zener operation in reverse breakdown
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 72–73 and 75–76 cover semiconductor junctions and device families, with a brief treatment of specialty diodes. They cannot alone establish full Zener and SCR competence.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Identify the role of the junction and distinguish a regulator diode from a switching/controlled device; use Alfred for datasheet limits.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Linear regulators and headroom
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 85–89 cover transformer and rectifier supply blocks, filtering, ripple and regulation.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Sketch rectifier → filter → regulator and identify how a poor capacitor or regulator changes output ripple.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Measuring gain without fooling yourself
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: The selected pages discuss amplifier classes, push-pull operation and decibel power ratios; they are not a direct step-by-step treatment of modern op-amp inverting gain.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Compare amplifier class behavior and solve the book dB gain example; then use Alfred for the inverting op-amp formula.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Place value: one quantity, different bases
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 132–140 introduce base conversions, logic gates, binary operations and sequential logic. This broad selection spans several lessons.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Convert a number in binary/octal/hex, then explain one truth table and one sequential behavior without looking.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: CPU blocks and control flow
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 149–150 describe computer architecture, processor operations, instructions and memory addressing.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Trace a basic instruction fetch/decode/execute sequence and identify what changes in memory or registers.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Copper pair, coaxial and optical signal paths
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: The inherited pp.108–109 emphasize antennas and the ionosphere; pp.109–110 directly introduce coax cable charts, shields, center conductors and characteristic signal-path properties. The corrected selection is still only partial cabling coverage.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Using pp.109–110, explain the center conductor, dielectric and shield. Use Alfred and current cable standards for crimp, bonding and fiber practice.

readingPassageTopicReview.currentLessonTitle: Photocells, photodiodes and photovoltaic sources
readingPassageTopicReview.sourceEvidence: Printed page 77 discusses light-responsive semiconductor devices including phototransistors. This does not fully cover modern LCD/OLED displays or optical sensors.
readingPassageTopicReview.guidedRetrievalTask: Distinguish photodiode, phototransistor and photovoltaic functions; separately review modern displays in Alfred.
